summary: The reviewed research does not establish a qualifying benefit for this product's assessed use. Existing human research is kept: Cs-4 (exploratory threshold signals after a null overall comparison) and PeakO2 (multi-mushroom, exploratory 3-week extension), plus the 2024 muscle-tissue study in 14 adults (not endurance, strength or meaningful recovery). Per Dr. Pham's 2026-10-28 ruling (no generic stamina credit, not 'all trials null'), the two approved non-scoring contexts (Cs-4 20804368; PeakO2 27408987) stay unchanged. The 2024 study 38501161 (abstract only; the CC-BY publisher PDF returned HTTP 403) gave 14 young adults a single 1 g Cordyceps sinensis dose before interval exercise and reports earlier muscle stem-cell recruitment: a tissue-biomarker finding with no performance outcome, approved without credit. The record becomes reference-only, which removes Cordyceps Evidence points from dependent products, and its notes now describe 38501161 instead of listing it as a pending task.

record_updates.notes: Cs-4 PMID20804368 has an overall null between-group comparison; favorable threshold changes are exploratory within-group findings. PeakO2 PMID27408987 is a six-mushroom preparation, with a one-week null comparison and exploratory extension. PMID38501161 (2024, 14 adults, single 1 g Cordyceps sinensis dose) reports earlier muscle stem-cell recruitment and attenuated necrotic infiltration after exercise: tissue biomarkers only, no performance outcome. These sources do not establish generic Cordyceps efficacy, a shared dose threshold or functional recovery. Per Dr. Pham's 2026-10-28 ruling: no generic stamina credit; the evidence is not uniformly null (Cs-4 exploratory signals, PeakO2 multi-mushroom extension, 2024 biomarker study).
